subject: chewing gum
title: What If You Chewed Gum All Day, Every Day?

scenes.text: What if you chewed gum all day? Your jaw isn't the part that complains first.
In a small Mayo Clinic study, fast chewing burned about 11 extra calories an hour. Not much.
Every chew also swallows a little air, and by evening that means bloating and gas.
Hours of chewing tire the jaw muscles, and can bring clicking, headaches and jaw pain.
Then the sweetener. Sorbitol in sugar-free gum isn't fully digested, so it pulls water into your gut.
Doctors described two people chewing about 15 sticks or more a day: months of diarrhea, and one lost 22 kilos. Weight loss, for the worst reason.

description:
What if you chewed gum all day? A 1999 Mayo Clinic study found fast chewing burns about 11 extra calories an hour; constant chewing also means swallowed air, bloating and possible jaw pain.
In a 2008 BMJ report, two patients eating 18 to 30 grams of sorbitol a day, much of it from sugar-free gum, had chronic diarrhea and lost 11 and 22 kg; both recovered on a sorbitol-free diet.
